findings.text: follow-on: _UNIT_TOKEN_RE and _NUMERIC_INTERVAL_RE at :67-68 and the predicate at :102 re-implement doc_links.py:95 _is_prose_bracket, the owner of the notation exclusion, which this runner already imports from the same gate worktree; the copy also reproduces the branch doc_links.py:107-109 renders unreachable, so the census's zero measures the copy rather than the owner and goes stale if the owner changes.

follow-on: the notation_should_be_excluded class at :224 cannot come out non-zero - its members are the phrases returned by find_prose_bracket_phrases, which at doc_links.py:131-132 emits only phrases that pass _is_prose_bracket - so the HTML's claim at :63 and :152 that 0 flagged phrase is a unit or interval is a restatement of the selecting predicate and is not evidence the exclusions work.

follow-on: dd_link_syntax_positive_control carries no 'passed' key (census.log:11 prints passed= None) and exercises only the gate's link-target regex, so nothing shows the CONTAINS 'dd:' scan at :139-144 - which returns the node's load-bearing zero, 0 of 2530 accepted documents - can see a dd: token known to be present.

follow-on: the 'other' class is counted but neither its reason string nor its document ids are recorded, so the HTML's explanation at :75 that the 10 are math brackets followed by a parenthesised argument is an assertion the JSON cannot be checked against; the reason at docs_gates.py:531 is 'link has an unsupported target or an empty label' and the runner discards it.

follow-on: four §1 citations point at the wrong statement - _extract_links_from_docs is cited as graph_ops.py:513 but its def is at graph_ops.py:522 (513 is _DD_LINK_RE), the same :513 is cited again at :141 for the 'self-loop is meaningless' docstring that sits at graph_ops.py:536, _LINK_RE (:509) and _DD_LINK_RE (:515) are at 505 and 513, and _compute_link_status (:490) is at 492 - so a reader following any of them lands on a different symbol in a deliverable whose evidence is its citations.

follow-on: _BARE_BRACKET_RE is cited as doc_links.py:25 both here and at :181, but the constant is defined at doc_links.py:20 in the prose-link worktree, in the census worktree and on main; the pattern is also quoted without its leading (?<![!\A-Za-z0-9_]) guard, which is the clause that keeps the node's argument about masked spans intact.

item_verdicts.diff: read the three commits against base c5b7f76ed commit by commit: 76aaabb98 adds the runner (383 lines) and the JSON (1054), a24e1d818 rewrites the JSON in place after a formatter mangled it (+1056/-1046), 0d18022e0 adds the HTML fragment (204).
item_verdicts.done_when: the review brief's done-when asks for the JSON written by the runner with a log ending EXIT=0 plus the fragment answering all three questions with cited lines, per-class counts and examples; census.log:13 ends in EXIT=0, srtj-docs-bracket-census.json records documents_read 2530 and class_counts {bare_prose_bracket 613, self_link 24, others 0/0/0/10}, and the fragment carries five verbatim examples per class.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to diagnose the 637 accepted documents the prose-link rule would newly fail - quote the future-name convention, classify every failing bracket, trace the writer of the bare phrases; srtj-docs-bracket-census.html:20-43 quotes syntax, writer, swapper and reader, :45-63 carries the per-class table and :152-190 traces the writer to generate_docs_system.md:315-321 and _normalize_bare_doc_links.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states status complete, records the gate command, the census log path, the imported gate module path, the headline counts and the three per-class resolutions, and names the 10 unsupported-target documents and the single-token _BARE_BRACKET_RE gap as follow-ons.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source manifest declares three write paths under docs/evidence/fragments/sn-review-through-jev/; the diff at c5b7f76ed..0d18022e0 touches exactly those three files (census-run.py, census.json, census.html) and no other.

justifications.durability: no test exists and none was in scope; the durable artefact is the re-runnable runner, whose controls at srtj-docs-bracket-census-run.py:196-290 fail if the prose scanner or the gate stops firing, but the dd: zero at :139-144 and the notation class at :224 cannot redden on any regression.
justifications.evidence: srtj-docs-bracket-census.json records the measurement, its positive controls and the gate module path, and census.log:13 ends EXIT=0; but the load-bearing zero (0 of 2530 documents contain 'dd:') has no positive control that the CONTAINS scan can see a token known present, and the notation class is 0 by construction.
justifications.fit: the three files match the sibling evidence-fragment idiom (a *-run.py, its JSON and its HTML) and the mandated file name, and the naming checks over the three changed paths return no plan label; only refine_docs_user.md:185 is cited one line off at srtj-docs-bracket-census.html:173.
justifications.goal_fidelity: srtj-docs-bracket-census.html:20-43 answers Q1 with the four defining sites and :45-63 answers Q2 with per-class counts, but four of the §1 code citations (graph_ops.py:490, :509, :513, :515) point a few lines off the symbols they name.
justifications.reuse: srtj-docs-bracket-census-run.py:67-68 and :102 re-implement the gate's own notation exclusion, doc_links.py:95 _is_prose_bracket with its regexes at doc_links.py:24-25, which the runner already imports from that same worktree, and duplicate the unreachable numeric-interval branch a sibling review flagged at doc_links.py:109.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff at c5b7f76ed..0d18022e0 changes only srtj-docs-bracket-census-run.py, srtj-docs-bracket-census.json and srtj-docs-bracket-census.html, the three paths the manifest declares and the brief's write scope names.
